settings.c2pa_desc: Images Javis creates carry a provenance mark (Content Credentials) saying they were AI-generated. Facebook reads it to put an "AI-generated" label on posts. Strip the mark and the label usually stops showing, but you remain responsible for disclosing AI content under the law and the platform's terms wherever you post. The javisos.com author label is always kept either way.

ol.title: Run AI models on your own machine
ol.desc: Ollama runs open-weight models (Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek...) fully offline, free, with no request limits. Javis talks to it over the network, so the machine running Ollama does not have to be the one running Javis.
ol.note_native: Javis is running directly on this machine, so installing Ollama right here is enough.
ol.note_docker: Javis is running inside Docker, so "this machine" is the container, not yours. Install Ollama on YOUR real machine and put its address in the field below (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:11434).
ol.step_install: Install Ollama on the machine that will run the models
ol.confirm_change: Disconnect the current Ollama so you can enter a different address? Models already downloaded stay on that machine.
ol.specs_title: Specs of the machine running Ollama
ol.specs_unknown: Javis does not know that machine's specs, so it is recommending at a safe level. Ollama does not report the RAM or GPU of the machine it runs on, so if yours is stronger, enter it here.
ol.specs_hint: What you enter wins over what Javis reads, even when Ollama runs on this very machine.
ol.rec_sub: within its limits, best fit first

ol.dk_title: Three steps, on the SERVER itself, not in Javis's terminal
ol.dk_b1: SSH into the VPS as root. Javis's own terminal will not do: it runs inside the container, has no root, and anything installed there is wiped on the next update.
ol.dk_b3: Make Ollama listen on the Docker bridge address. Only containers on this host can reach it and nothing is exposed to the Internet, so no firewall step is needed:
ol.dk_b4: The address is already filled in below - just press Connect:
ol.dk_canh_bao: The command above binds Ollama to an internal address, so no firewall is needed. Only if you must use OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 (unusual Docker network) does Ollama listen to the whole Internet, and it has NO password: run ufw allow from THE-BRIDGE-SUBNET to any port 11434 then ufw deny 11434, or block port 11434 in your VPS provider's firewall.
ol.dk_cham: A VPS usually has no GPU and little RAM, so a CPU-bound model will be very slow. Your desktop at home (with a GPU, ideally) is the better host, at the cost of the VPS having to reach it.
ol.dk_khong_do_duoc: Javis could not work out the host address. Run the command below on the host, then put the number that follows the word default into the box above, with :11434 after it.
ol.dk_chan_doan: Still not connecting? On the host run: ss -ltnp | grep 11434. No line means Ollama is not running (see systemctl status ollama). A line with 127.0.0.1 means step 3 has not been done.
ol.set_main_ok: {ten} is now the main model. The model bar under the chat box has switched.
ol.canh_bao_cong_khai: Connected, but this is a public Internet address and Ollama has NO password, so anyone who knows it can use your models. Firewall port 11434 so only the Javis server can reach it.
ol.embed_note: Embedding model: makes search vectors, cannot answer. Javis has no use for this type yet.
